Article 257d of the Swiss Code of Obligations (OR) is the governing provision. It allows termination for unpaid rent or ancillary charges, but requires a two-stage procedure: first a written payment demand with a termination warning, then a separate termination if the arrears remain unpaid after the deadline.

Unemployment, financial hardship and having children do not suspend the payment deadline. Moreover, Article 272a(1)(a) OR excludes a judicial extension of the tenancy (Erstreckung) following a valid termination under Article 257d.
The practical priority is therefore to secure payment or an express agreement with the landlord before the deadline expires, while checking the demand’s validity.
